title: War stories
summary: A humorous anecdote from the early Usenet era, circulated in a computer-humor notefile and later collected in the Humor folders of Brad Templeton's jokes archive. It is narrated by a consultant brought in to fix a VAX minicomputer hidden inside a huge financial institution's IBM mainframe data center. The machine is small and sensitive, and the Comptroller, a tiny elderly gnome-like executive, has grown uneasy with the VAX staff's unconventional look. The consultant tries to teach the IBM operators the HELP command, bootstraps a rebooting habit, and labors to keep the VAX running. The story builds toward a disastrous power failure, a cascade of backup systems, a halon fire-suppression discharge, and a last twist in which the forgotten VAX is the only machine that survives. The piece is a satire of corporate computing culture and the clash between IBM and VAX practices, with running jokes about reboots and cheat sheets. It was written in 1987 and remains a classic of humorous computing lore.
